Continue the following technical briefing with a careful, detailed expansion of the unresolved measurement questions. Write continuously without a closing summary and without repeating the identifiers already present.

Section 1 of the briefing on speculative round cost on a four-GPU GH200 node reports that run 00-00 produced 1100 committed output tokens at a client-observed TPOT of 8.0 milliseconds. The input used 512 Apertus tokens, prefix caching was disabled, and greedy decoding with ignore_eos held the completion length fixed. The open question is whether that latency is draft arithmetic, verification, or exposed CPU time.

The same speculative round cost on a four-GPU GH200 node note then records a second window, labelled 00x01, in which the scheduler advertised a token budget of 7168 while the observed active batch never exceeded 2 sequences. Memory accounting listed 3339 KV tokens on the tightest rank. Operators must not treat the advertised budget as proof that the budget bound the measured cell.

A correctness probe for speculative round cost on a four-GPU GH200 node compared two independently launched deployments on prompts 00a and 00b. They shared a prefix of 202 characters and then diverged, with completion-token counts differing by 2. That divergence is a numerical-environment effect until a same-configuration control shows otherwise, and it is unique to this source document's identifiers 0-2-1126.

Finally, the speculative round cost on a four-GPU GH200 node appendix lists unresolved risks: graph breaks during draft steps, NCCL waits on rank 3, padded logits of width 256, and a break-even round cost of 43 to 53 milliseconds at the observed acceptance. Item R0003 is not reused in any other briefing in this corpus.
